chapter: Miss Wen, You Really Know How to Handle People
subtitle: 温姑娘，你也太会做人了
sentences: Early the next morning, I went straight to Wen Li's lodgings.
I'd meant to tell her about the two hundred taels the moment I stepped inside. But the door had barely opened a crack when an unfamiliar older servant gave me a thorough once-over.
"Who are you here to see, Miss Jiang?"
"Wen Li."
"Miss Wen is entertaining a visitor."
"I count as a visitor too, don't I?"
The woman looked distinctly uncomfortable. "The lady who just went in is here to collect a debt."
That got my attention at once.
So even the heroine of the original novel couldn't escape debt collectors after escaping her wedding.

When I entered the courtyard, Wen Li was talking to the manager of an embroidery workshop. She wore a faded blue-green dress, its color washed almost away. A dozen old embroidery patterns lay across the table. She wore no jewelry, only a red thread around her wrist.

The manager slapped an invoice. "Miss Wen, our workshop has been taking orders from your family for four years. When have we ever been paid in less than three months? With the Wen family in this state, you owe us a straight answer!"
Wen Li didn't argue. She simply slid a sheet of paper across the table.
"My mother paid a deposit on those eight bolts of embroidered silk the year before last. Deduct that from what we owe you. I'll take responsibility for the balance."
The manager flipped through her records for a long while. Her expression shifted.
"How did you know about that payment?"
"My mother taught me to keep accounts while she was alive."
"But these embroidery patterns—"
"Take them back and sell them. There'll be buyers. I drew these few myself; if they're worth anything, put that toward the debt too."
The manager held the sheet between her fingers, then let out a long sigh.
"Miss Wen, I'm not trying to make your life difficult."

"I know." Wen Li topped up her tea. "You have embroiderers to pay as well. I can give you twenty percent today and settle the rest in monthly installments. If you'd feel safer, we'll put it in writing."
After a long silence, the manager finally nodded.
I stood to one side, absolutely dumbstruck.
Only after the woman had left did I ask, "How can you remember the workshop's old accounts down to the last detail?"
Wen Li rolled up the patterns.
"Because I'm poor."
"If I didn't keep track, people would overcharge me."
There was something so painfully practical about that answer that I couldn't think of a single word to say.
I sat down across from her. "There's something I need to tell you. You might not like hearing it."
"Who have you put in a bridal sedan chair this time?"
"Wen Li!"
She smiled. I wasn't in the mood to trade barbs, though, so I told her everything about the two hundred taels Mother had taken.
She listened carefully without interrupting once. When I finished, her first question was, "Is your mother willing to explain it to the Ministry of Punishments?"
"Yes. She's going there with Uncle Qin this afternoon."
Wen Li let out a small breath of relief.
That irritated me. "Don't you have anything else to say?"
"Such as?"
"A little comfort, maybe? I wasn't the one who took the money, but I barely slept a wink last night."
She considered that seriously. "Jiang Mingyue, you really don't have much luck."
"...That's not the sort of comfort I meant."
"Then I'll tell you what I actually think."
She set down the embroidery patterns and looked me in the eye.

"If your mother had signed a false delivery receipt, I'd have handed that over too. The fact that she refused to sign doesn't make taking the money and keeping quiet harmless. You choosing to tell me about it matters more than you yelling at Xie Linzhou for me at the marquis's residence."
I stared down at my teacup, turning it idly between my fingers.
She went on. "My father signed a handover document he knew had problems. If the investigation shows that he really did something wrong, I can't ask someone else to take the blame for him."
Hearing that from her hurt more than hearing the same thing from Gu Huaichuan.
I raised my head. "Aren't you afraid your father won't come home?"
"I am."
"Then why keep investigating?"
"Because if I don't, all he can do is wait for Xie Linzhou to be in a generous mood."
I looked at her and suddenly couldn't decide whom I was still angry with.
"Wen Li."
"Yes?"
"I still don't trust you completely."
"I know."
"But I didn't come here today to call off our partnership."
Her eyes dropped to the patterns. She slowly smoothed a crease with her fingertips.
"Then we won't call it off. Not yet."
We looked at each other for a long moment—and both burst out laughing.

That afternoon, Chuntao brought me a receipt from the Ministry of Punishments. Mother really had gone to the office with Uncle Qin. She had submitted the deposit slip for the two hundred taels, along with a written account of how the money had come into her hands, and left her name so she could be questioned. Gu Huaichuan hadn't declared her innocent. He had only said he would verify who sent the money and check the records from that year.
Wen Li read the receipt, folded it neatly, and handed it back.
"Keep that. If anyone asks later, you'll have proof your mother didn't merely talk about coming clean at home."
I tucked it into my sleeve. "Are you praising my mother, or reminding me to keep a paper trail?"
"Both."
We could laugh about it, but there were still accounts to settle.
"Who actually got that account book out of the marquis's residence?" I asked. "I've asked you several times. You can't keep me in the dark forever."
Wen Li didn't quite follow the second part, but she understood the first.
She got up, shut the window, and took out a tiny piece of paper folded into a triangle. A single character was written on it: Zhou.

"Nanny Zhou. She isn't the study maid you took her for. She used to be in charge of the marquis's old archives. Every ledger returned to storage and every old volume taken out to be aired went through her hands."
"So Xie Linzhou trusted her to look after his private accounts?"

"No. Two days before the wedding, the steward ordered the archive staff to move a batch of old books from Xie Linzhou's study for inventory. Nanny Zhou recognized his private ledger while helping move them. She was responsible for recording the books, not their owner, but that gave her a chance to get her hands on it."
"And she just walked off with the whole book?"

Wen Li nodded. "She replaced it with an old blank volume that had a similar cover. It was the only way she could think of. Once the ledger went missing, the first people they'd question would be the ones who moved the books. She knew that better than anyone."
I sucked in a breath. "Then why take such a risk?"
Instead of answering directly, Wen Li drew an old prescription from her sleeve.

"Her son was once apprenticed at the government granary. Someone tried to force him to testify to a grain receipt that wasn't true. My father told him to return to his village first, and he escaped that ordeal. Nanny Zhou never forgot it."
"So she did all this to repay a favor?"

"Not entirely. Her son never dared work in the grain trade again, and the family has been living on her wages alone. She said that if those people were allowed to rewrite the accounts once more, there was no telling how many others would pay the price."
I thought for a moment. "Then was she the one who knocked three times on the Wen house's back window on the wedding day?"

"No. She was still at the marquis's residence and couldn't leave. That was A-Qin, an embroidery-workshop assistant I'd sent to collect something. She waited in the side alley, received the ledger that Nanny Zhou had sent out through someone else, and hurried it over to the Wen house."
"And the note under my teacup in Chapter Four?"
"Nanny Zhou sent that as well, through Auntie Yuan, who served the tea. She didn't dare leave the residence herself."
At last, those scattered pieces clicked into place.
"So Nanny Zhou knew all along that you meant to run away from the wedding?"
"All she knew was that I planned to take the ledger to the Ministry of Punishments on the wedding day." Wen Li shook her head. "I didn't tell her I also planned to make you the bride."
"That much I believe," I said with a chilly smile. "I didn't find out myself until they practically put me in the bridal chair."
Wen Li wouldn't meet my eyes. Instead, she refilled my tea.
"Don't even try," I said. "More tea won't make up for that."
Just then, someone knocked sharply at the door.
A-Qin hurried inside. She was in her early twenties, with faint calluses from embroidery needles on her fingers, and her face had gone white.
"Miss Wen, they've added two shifts of guards at the rear gate. The archives are checking everyone who handled that batch of old books. Nanny Zhou asked me to pass on a message."
She pushed a crumpled note into Wen Li's hand.
It wasn't a plea to be rescued. It said only: Uncle Feng has had a fever for three days. We're out of medicine. Men at the back gate. Do not come.
"Who's Uncle Feng?" I asked.
"Her husband," Wen Li said quietly. "He's been ill for some time. They live in the rear servants' quarters."
The Jiang family's vegetable cart immediately sprang to mind.
"We're delivering vegetables to the rear alley tomorrow," I said. "Couldn't we find some way to get them out?"
A-Qin's head jerked up. "What if you two get caught?"
"That's why we won't do anything yet." Wen Li laid a hand over mine. "We don't even know who's guarding that gate or when the shifts change. We can't gamble Nanny Zhou's whole family on a guess."
I opened my mouth, then closed it.
Wen Li looked straight at me. "Jiang Mingyue, what did you promise last time?"
I answered reluctantly. "If someone else has to take the risk, ask what they want before deciding for them."
"Good. You do remember."
Wen Li turned the old prescription over, wrote two lines on the back, and gave it to A-Qin.
"Find out how ill Uncle Feng is. If the fever really won't break, I'll send for a doctor. As for whether Nanny Zhou wants to leave or stay, let her tell us herself."
A-Qin took the paper but didn't leave right away.
"Miss Wen," she asked hesitantly, "what if she says she won't go?"
Wen Li glanced at me.
"Then we'll start by finding a way to keep her from risking her life over a bowl of medicine."
I felt the cart pass tucked in my sleeve. Suddenly, this seemed harder than switching brides had been.
On the day of the wedding, nobody had asked whether I wanted to climb into that bridal chair.
This time, we would have to start by asking whether everyone actually wanted to be saved.
translations: 第二天一早，我先去了温梨的住处。
我本想一进门就把两百两的事说了，结果门才开了一条缝，一个陌生婆子便上下打量我。
“姜姑娘来找谁？”
“温梨。”
“姑娘正在见客。”
“我也算客吧？”
婆子一脸为难：“刚才进去那位，是来讨债的。”
我顿时来了精神。
原来这位原著女主逃婚以后，也逃不过催账。
我进院时，温梨正在跟绣坊掌柜说话。她穿一身洗得发白的青衣，桌上摊着十几张旧绣样，没戴首饰，只有腕上一根红绳。
掌柜拍着账单说：“姑娘，我们绣坊给温家做了四年活，哪回不是三个月才结？如今温家的事闹成这样，姑娘总得给句准话！”
温梨没争辩，只将一张纸推过去。
“前年的八匹绣缎，是我娘先付的定钱。您把那笔定钱从账里扣了，剩下的由我认。”
掌柜翻了半天，脸色变了变。
“你怎么知道那笔钱？”
“我娘在世时教过我记账。”
“可这些绣样——”
“您拿回去卖吧，市面上不愁买主。这几张是我自己画的，若还能卖钱，也一并抵账。”
掌柜捏着纸，最后长长叹了口气。
“温姑娘，我不是非要难为你。”
“我知道。”温梨替她添了茶，“您也要给绣娘发工钱。我今日先给两成，剩下的按月还。您若觉得不稳妥，我们立字据。”
掌柜沉默半晌，终于点了头。
我在一旁看得目瞪口呆。
等人走远，我才问：“你怎么连绣坊的旧账都记得？”
温梨把绣样卷起来。
“因为我穷。”
“以前不记，会被人多算。”
这理由朴素得让我一句话也接不上。
我在她对面坐下：“我有件事要告诉你，可能不太好听。”
“你又把谁送上花轿了？”
“温梨！”
她笑了一下。我却没心思跟她斗嘴，把李氏两百两的事从头说了。
她听得很仔细，中间没打断我。直到我说完，她才问：“你娘愿意去刑部说明吗？”
“愿意。她约了秦叔午后去。”
温梨轻轻松了口气。
我不乐意了：“你就没什么别的话想说？”
“比如？”
“比如安慰我两句。这两百两不是我收的，可我昨晚一夜没睡好。”
她想了想，认真道：“姜明月，你运气确实不怎么样。”
“……我不是要这种安慰。”
“那我说真话。”
她把绣样放下，看着我。
“若你娘真补签了假回执，我会把那份回执也交出去。她没补签，不代表收钱和瞒事便无关紧要。你愿意把这事告诉我，比你在侯府替我骂谢临舟有用。”
我低头玩着茶盏。
她接着说：“我父亲也签过自己明知有问题的交接书。将来要是查出他确实做错了事，我也不能让别人替他担着。”
这话从她嘴里说出来，比从顾怀川嘴里听到更让我难受。
我抬起头：“你不怕你爹回不来？”
“那你还查？”
“因为不查，他就只能等谢临舟心情好。”
我看着她，忽然不知道该继续生谁的气。
“温梨。”
“我还是没完全信你。”
“我知道。”
“但我今天来，不是要跟你散伙。”
她垂着眼，指尖慢慢抚平绣样上的折痕。
“那就先不散。”
我们两个对望半天，同时笑了。
午后，春桃送来一张刑部的收讫凭据。我娘果然与秦叔一道去了衙门，把那笔两百两的存单和来龙去脉写成陈述递上去，留下姓名备讯。顾怀川没说她无罪，只说要核对送钱人的身份与当年的账。
温梨看过凭据，仔细折好还给我。
“收着吧。往后有人问起，你娘不是只在家里说了说。”
我把纸塞进袖子：“你这是表扬我娘，还是在提醒我做事要留凭据？”
“都有。”
笑归笑，该算的账还是得算。
“账册到底是谁从侯府送出来的？”我问，“我问了你好几次，总不能一直这样瞒着吧？”
温梨没听懂后半句，却听懂了前半句。
她起身关好窗，取出一张小纸条，折成三角，上面写着一个“周”字。
“周嬷嬷。她不是你以为的管书房的丫鬟，原先管侯府旧档房。旧账归库、旧册翻晒，都要经她的手。”
“所以谢临舟把私账交给她保管？”
“没有。大婚前两日，侯府管事让档房的人把谢临舟书房里一批积年的旧册送去清点。周嬷嬷跟着搬册子时认出了那本私账。她只负责登记，不是书房主人，但有机会摸到那本书。”
“她就把整本拿走了？”
温梨点头：“她换回去一本封皮相近的空旧册。那是她能想到的办法。账册失踪之后，府里第一个要查的就是搬过书的人，她比谁都清楚。”
我倒抽一口凉气：“那她为什么还敢做？”
温梨没有直接回答，而是从袖中抽出一张旧药方。
“她儿子当年给官仓做过学徒。有人要逼他在不实的收粮单上作证。我父亲让他先回乡，躲过了一劫。周嬷嬷一直记着。”
“就为了报恩？”
“也不全是。她儿子后来没敢再碰粮行的差事，家里靠她一个人的月钱撑着。她说，要是再让那帮人把账改一遍，将来还不知要赔进去多少人。”
我想了想：“大婚那天，温府后窗有人敲三下，就是她？”
“不是。她人在侯府，出不来。那是我安排去取东西的绣坊伙计阿芹。她提前等在侧巷，接过周嬷嬷托人递出来的账册，再赶去温府。”
“那第四章茶盏底下的纸呢？”
“也是周嬷嬷托送茶的袁婶带给你的。她不敢自己离开侯府。”
我终于把这几件事接在了一起。
“所以周嬷嬷从一开始就知道你会逃婚？”
“她只知道我要在大婚那天拿着账去刑部。”温梨摇头，“我没告诉她，我还打算拿你当新娘。”
“这点我倒是信。”我冷笑，“毕竟我本人也是临上花轿才知道。”
温梨不敢看我，拿茶壶给我续满了杯。
“少来。”我说，“赔茶也没用。”
这时，门外传来急促的敲门声。
阿芹跑了进来。她二十出头，指头上带着绣针磨出来的薄茧，脸色白得厉害。
“姑娘，侯府后门多了两班人，档房正在查谁动过那批旧册。周嬷嬷让我带句话。”
她将一张揉皱的纸塞进温梨手里。
纸上不是求救，只写着：冯叔发热三日，药断了。后门有人。勿来。
“冯叔是谁？”我问。
“她丈夫。”温梨低声说，“一直卧病，在侯府后排住着。”
我脑子里立刻冒出姜家的送菜车。
“明日菜车要送进后巷，”我说，“能不能想办法把他们接出来？”
阿芹猛地抬头：“二位姑娘若被抓了怎么办？”
“所以先别动。”温梨按住我的手，“我们连后门守谁、怎么换班都不知道，不能把周嬷嬷一家押上去赌。”
我张了张嘴。
她看着我：“姜明月，你上次答应的是什么？”
我不情不愿地答：“涉及别人冒险，先让人自己决定。”
“记得就好。”
温梨翻过那张药方，写了两行字交给阿芹。
“问清冯叔病成什么样；若真高热不退，我去请大夫。周嬷嬷想走还是想留下，让她自己回话。”
阿芹接过纸，却没有立刻走。
“姑娘，”她迟疑着问，“她要是说不走呢？”
温梨看了一眼我。
“那我们就先想办法，让她不必因为一碗药把命搭进去。”
我摸了摸袖里的车牌，忽然发现这次比替嫁还难。
替嫁那天，没人问我愿不愿意上花轿。
这一次，倒是得先问清楚每个人愿不愿意被救。

annotations.explain: early加在时间短语前表示很早，the next morning在叙事中承接前一晚。
annotations.example: Early the next morning, the shop opened again.

annotations.explain: go straight to强调不绕路、不先做别的事，straight修饰动作方向。
annotations.example: She went straight to the station.

annotations.explain: had meant to常表示过去原有打算未能按计划实现。
annotations.example: I'd meant to call, but I forgot.

annotations.explain: the moment作连词相当于as soon as，后接完整分句。
annotations.example: Call me the moment you arrive.

annotations.phrase: had barely opened a crack when
annotations.explain: had barely done ... when表示前一个动作刚发生，另一个动作便紧接着发生。
annotations.example: I'd barely sat down when the phone rang.

annotations.meaning: 把我从头到脚打量了一番
annotations.explain: give someone the once-over是口语固定表达，强调快速审视；thorough增强审视的仔细程度。
annotations.example: The guard gave my bag a once-over.

annotations.phrase: Who are you here to see
annotations.explain: be here to do说明来此的目的，Who是see的宾语前置。
annotations.example: Who are you here to meet?

annotations.explain: entertain除了娱乐还可指在家或工作场所招待、接待来客。
annotations.example: They're entertaining visitors this afternoon.

annotations.phrase: I count as a visitor too
annotations.explain: count as意为被视为、算作，常用来讨论是否符合某个类别。
annotations.example: Does a phone call count as a meeting?

annotations.explain: distinctly修饰形容词，表示明显、清楚地，并非一定是截然不同。
annotations.example: She looked distinctly annoyed.

annotations.explain: collect a debt是常用金融与生活搭配，区别于pay a debt偿还债务。
annotations.example: The company hired someone to collect the debt.

annotations.explain: get someone's attention表达吸引注意，at once是立即。
annotations.example: The sudden noise got everyone's attention.

annotations.explain: escape后面可以直接接名词，表摆脱某人或某事，而非只能表示从地点逃跑。
annotations.example: She couldn't escape the reporters.

annotations.explain: after + doing表示完成某动作之后，两个escape连接幽默反差。
annotations.example: After finishing dinner, he went out.

annotations.explain: wear away表示磨损、褪去；这里用过去分词描写衣物颜色的状态。
annotations.example: The lettering had worn away.

annotations.explain: lie–lay–lain意为平躺、处于某处，lay在这里是过去式，不是lay–laid–laid放置。
annotations.example: An old map lay across the table.

annotations.phrase: only a red thread around her wrist
annotations.explain: only强调唯一的饰物，around her wrist表示围绕手腕的位置。
annotations.example: She wore a thin bracelet around her wrist.

annotations.explain: slap可接纸张等物体，表现急躁、施压或强调观点。
annotations.example: He slapped the contract on the desk.

annotations.explain: take orders from在商业语境指接受客户订单，另一种语境也可指听从指示。
annotations.example: The bakery takes orders from hotels.

annotations.explain: less than后接数量，强调低于某个界限。
annotations.example: The repairs were finished in less than a week.

annotations.explain: in this state在此指处境或状况，不是国家或州的意思。
annotations.example: You can't work in this state.

annotations.meaning: 该给我们一个明确答复
annotations.explain: owe someone an answer是欠对方一个交代；straight answer指不兜圈子的答复。
annotations.example: I think you owe her a straight answer.

annotations.explain: argue不一定指吵架，也可指提出反对理由；这里表现温梨选择以账据回应。
annotations.example: He didn't argue with the decision.

annotations.phrase: slid a sheet of paper across the table
annotations.explain: slide something across强调平滑推送；sheet of paper是单张纸的常见量词结构。
annotations.example: She slid the note across the desk.

annotations.explain: pay a deposit on常用于商品、租赁或预订；deposit在此不是银行存款。
annotations.example: We paid a deposit on the apartment.

annotations.explain: the year before last是固定时间表达；last year才是去年。
annotations.example: We met the year before last.

annotations.explain: deduct A from B指从B扣去A，方向与中文语序不同。
annotations.example: Deduct the discount from the total.

annotations.explain: take responsibility for表示承担责任；balance在账务中是余款而非平衡。
annotations.example: I'll take responsibility for the remaining balance.

annotations.explain: flip through强调较快地逐页翻看，records在此为账册记录。
annotations.example: I flipped through the old photos.

annotations.explain: expression shifted用微妙的变化暗示发现或情绪转折。
annotations.example: His expression shifted when he saw the name.

annotations.explain: How did you know about询问消息来源，区别于How do you know that表达对判断依据的追问。
annotations.example: How did you know about the meeting?

annotations.explain: keep accounts是财务固定搭配，account在这里通常用复数。
annotations.example: My aunt taught me to keep accounts.

annotations.explain: while引导时间从句，was alive自然表示仍在世。
annotations.example: He lived with his grandmother while she was alive.

annotations.explain: take something back在此是取回物品，也可指撤回说过的话，要看宾语与语境。
annotations.example: You can take the book back tomorrow.

annotations.explain: There will be结构表示存在将来情况，非表示特定人物。
annotations.example: There'll be more chances next week.

annotations.explain: be worth something是有价值；anything用在条件句中表示任何可观的价值。
annotations.example: If it's worth anything, keep it.

annotations.explain: put money toward something指将钱用于某项目或偿还债务。
annotations.example: We put the refund toward rent.

annotations.explain: let out a sigh/laugh/cry表示发出某种声音，是小说常见动作搭配。
annotations.example: He let out a sigh of relief.

annotations.explain: make someone's life difficult是日常惯用表达，强调给人添麻烦。
annotations.example: I don't want to make your life difficult.

annotations.explain: top up指把杯子或容器添满，常用于茶、饮料、账户余额。
annotations.example: Can I top up your glass?

annotations.explain: have + 名词 + to do表示尚有待处理的义务或任务。
annotations.example: I have bills to pay.

annotations.explain: settle在账务语境指清偿、结算，rest指剩余部分。
annotations.example: We'll settle the rest next month.

annotations.explain: in installments是分期付款的常见表达，monthly指定每月。
annotations.example: The loan is repaid in monthly installments.

annotations.explain: put something in writing强调留下书面记录而非仅靠口头承诺。
annotations.example: Please put the agreement in writing.

annotations.explain: after + 名词短语也能表示时间先后，并非一定要接完整从句。
annotations.example: After a long pause, she replied.

annotations.explain: stand to one side表示站到旁边或保持旁观位置。
annotations.example: He stood to one side and watched.

annotations.explain: dumbstruck是因震惊而说不出话，absolutely加强程度。
annotations.example: I was dumbstruck by the news.

annotations.explain: down to the last detail表示精确到最细微处，不是真的向下。
annotations.example: She planned the trip down to the last detail.

annotations.explain: roll up用于卷起地图、纸张、袖子等，具体意义依宾语变化。
annotations.example: He rolled up the poster.

annotations.phrase: couldn't think of a single word to say
annotations.explain: couldn't think of表示想不出，a single加强“连一个都没有”。
annotations.example: I couldn't think of a single excuse.

annotations.explain: across from是位置介词短语，表示在对面。
annotations.example: The bank is across from the station.

annotations.explain: might表可能性，like hearing it用动名词表达喜欢听到某事。
annotations.example: You might not like what I'm about to say.

annotations.phrase: put in a bridal sedan chair
annotations.explain: put someone in something是使某人处于某处，温梨以旧事反讽姜明月。
annotations.example: Who put the keys in my bag?

annotations.explain: be in the mood to do是常见表达，否定式说明没兴致。
annotations.example: I'm not in the mood to argue.

annotations.explain: trade barbs表示你来我往地说尖刻话，不是字面交换倒刺。
annotations.example: The two rivals traded barbs on stage.

annotations.explain: without + doing表达未做某事，once在否定语境强调一次都没有。
annotations.example: She listened without interrupting once.

annotations.explain: 用first凸显人物关注重点，而不是照搬中文语序逐字翻译。
annotations.example: His first question was about the deadline.

annotations.explain: be willing to do强调主观愿意，不等于已经完成。
annotations.example: She is willing to discuss the issue.

annotations.phrase: let out a small breath of relief
annotations.explain: let out和breath of relief组合表示放松情绪。
annotations.example: I let out a breath of relief when he arrived.

annotations.explain: irritate是使某人烦躁，主语That指前面整件事而非某个具体人。
annotations.example: The delay irritated everyone.

annotations.explain: Such as?可单独用作口语追问例子，语气自然。
annotations.example: "We need supplies." "Such as?"

annotations.explain: not sleep a wink是固定习语，wink本义眨眼而非睡眠单位。
annotations.example: I didn't sleep a wink last night.

annotations.explain: consider something seriously是认真对待某事，也用于人物有意一本正经的幽默。
annotations.example: He considered the offer seriously.

annotations.explain: the sort of + 名词表示某类事物，用于指出期待与现实不一致。
annotations.example: That's not the sort of help I need.

annotations.explain: actually在此强调和客套话相对的真实想法。
annotations.example: I'll tell you what I actually think.

annotations.explain: look someone in the eye是直视对方的固定表达，常暗示认真、诚实或直面冲突。
annotations.example: She looked me in the eye and said no.

annotations.phrase: I'd have handed that over too
annotations.explain: would have + 过去分词表与过去事实相反的假设结果，此处搭配if从句。
annotations.example: If I'd found it, I'd have handed it over.

annotations.phrase: doesn't make taking the money and keeping quiet harmless
annotations.meaning: 不代表收钱和隐瞒就无关紧要
annotations.explain: make + 宾语 + 形容词表示使某事具备某性质，taking和keeping是并列动名词。
annotations.example: One good act doesn't make the mistake harmless.

annotations.explain: matter在这里是动词“重要”，more than用于比较。
annotations.example: Being honest matters more than looking perfect.

annotations.explain: yell at someone侧重对人吼叫，yell for help则是喊着求助。
annotations.example: Stop yelling at your brother.

annotations.phrase: turning it idly between my fingers
annotations.meaning: 在手指间漫不经心地转着
annotations.explain: 现在分词短语补充伴随动作，idly体现走神和复杂情绪。
annotations.example: He sat there, turning a pen idly.

annotations.explain: go on既可表示继续发生，也能作为对话中的“接着说”。
annotations.example: She paused, then went on.

annotations.phrase: shows that he really did something wrong
annotations.explain: show that引出调查结论，really did用助动词did加强肯定语气。
annotations.example: The test showed that the engine did fail.

annotations.explain: take the blame for是固定搭配，表示背锅或承担责任。
annotations.example: Don't take the blame for someone else's mistake.

annotations.explain: hurt可不接宾语表达情绪痛苦，more than连接比较项。
annotations.example: Losing the letter hurt more than losing the money.

annotations.explain: won't在此可表达未来结果，而不是单纯的拒绝回家。
annotations.example: I'm afraid he won't come home tonight.

annotations.explain: keep + doing表示持续进行某动作，比continue略口语。
annotations.example: Keep asking questions.

annotations.phrase: all he can do is wait
annotations.explain: all + 主语 + can do + is + 动词原形表示唯一能做的事。
annotations.example: All we can do is try.

annotations.explain: be in a ... mood表达某种心情；generous在此带对权势者随意施恩的讽刺。
annotations.example: The boss was in a generous mood.

annotations.explain: couldn't decide + 疑问词从句表示无法确定，whom是较正式的宾格。
annotations.example: I couldn't decide which one to take.

annotations.explain: not ... completely表达部分否定，不等于完全不信。
annotations.example: I don't completely agree with that.

annotations.explain: call off可指取消计划、活动或终止安排，partnership在此为双方合作。
annotations.example: They called off the meeting.

annotations.explain: smooth作为动词表示抚平，crease表示折痕或皱褶。
annotations.example: She smoothed the crease in her sleeve.

annotations.explain: Not yet既可表示尚未发生，也可婉转保留未来变化的可能。
annotations.example: "Are you leaving?" "Not yet."

annotations.explain: burst out + doing表示突然开始某动作，多用于笑、哭。
annotations.example: They burst out laughing at the joke.

annotations.explain: receipt在此为官署收讫凭据，而非超市小票，具体性质由from the Ministry限定。
annotations.example: Keep the receipt from the post office.

annotations.explain: along with表示与某物一起，语法上主语一致性通常由前面的核心名词决定。
annotations.example: She submitted a form along with her ID.

annotations.explain: come into someone's hands指某物经某途径到某人手中。
annotations.example: The letter came into his hands by chance.

annotations.phrase: left her name so she could be questioned
annotations.explain: so + 主语 + could引出目的，比单纯的so that更口语。
annotations.example: He left his number so we could call.

annotations.explain: declare someone + 形容词是作出正式认定，不能把收讫等同免责。
annotations.example: The court declared the contract invalid.

annotations.explain: verify后接wh-从句，表示核查待确认事实，不是接受其为真。
annotations.example: We must verify who signed the document.

annotations.explain: neatly表示整齐地、妥帖地；动词过去式加副词刻画人物习惯。
annotations.example: She folded the scarf neatly.

annotations.explain: come clean是主动承认隐瞒事实的常用习语。
annotations.example: He finally came clean about the mistake.

annotations.explain: if引出真实可能发生的条件，后面主句可用will。
annotations.example: If anyone asks, tell them I called.

annotations.explain: paper trail指能够追溯行为经过的书面或电子记录，不是字面纸张道路。
annotations.example: Keep a paper trail of all payments.

annotations.explain: Both可独立作答，承认前面提出的两个选项都成立。
annotations.example: "Tea or coffee?" "Both."

annotations.explain: settle accounts在本章一语双关，既指结账，也指把尚未解决的事弄清楚。
annotations.example: We still have a few accounts to settle.

annotations.phrase: got that account book out of
annotations.explain: get something out of表示把物品从某处取出，强调设法取得，不必然意味着合法或轻松。
annotations.example: How did you get the box out of the room?

annotations.explain: keep someone in the dark是高频习语，指不让某人知道重要信息。
annotations.example: Don't keep your team in the dark.

annotations.explain: can't keep + 宾语 + 状态表达对持续行为的反对。
annotations.example: You can't keep me waiting forever.

annotations.explain: follow在对话中可表示理解话语逻辑，not quite是部分否定、语气缓和。
annotations.example: Sorry, I didn't quite follow that.

annotations.explain: get up是高频短语动词，具体可指起床或站起来，需结合上下文。
annotations.example: She got up to close the door.

annotations.explain: 过去分词短语后置修饰paper，强调纸条现有状态。
annotations.example: He showed me a note folded into a square.

annotations.explain: take someone for someone/something指把某人认作某个身份。
annotations.example: I took him for the manager.

annotations.phrase: used to be in charge of
annotations.explain: used to do表示过去的惯常或身份，be in charge of表示负责管理。
annotations.example: She used to be in charge of sales.

annotations.explain: go through someone's hands形容材料在某人经手范围内流转，并非字面穿过手。
annotations.example: Every invoice goes through her hands.

annotations.explain: look after可指照看人或管理物品，在此不是“向后看”。
annotations.example: Could you look after these files?

annotations.explain: before + 时间事件说明参照节点，时间关系不可随意改成前一天。
annotations.example: We met two days before the exam.

annotations.phrase: ordered the archive staff to move
annotations.explain: order someone to do是命令结构；与ask someone to do语气不同。
annotations.example: The director ordered the staff to leave.

annotations.explain: a batch of用于一批同类物品，也可指一批处理的任务或商品。
annotations.example: We received a batch of documents.

annotations.explain: inventory既可指库存清单，也可指清点工作，for表示用途。
annotations.example: The goods were counted for inventory.

annotations.phrase: a chance to get her hands on it
annotations.explain: get one's hands on指设法拿到或接触某物，往往带有机会难得的意味。
annotations.example: I finally got my hands on the report.

annotations.explain: walk off with含未经允许拿走或轻而易举赢走的意味，语气比take更鲜明。
annotations.example: Someone walked off with my umbrella.

annotations.explain: the whole + 单数名词表示完整的一件事物。
annotations.example: She read the whole book overnight.

annotations.explain: replace A with B方向固定：B代替A。
annotations.example: Replace the broken part with a new one.

annotations.explain: similar通常搭配to，不能说similar with。
annotations.example: This edition has a similar cover to mine.

annotations.phrase: It was the only way she could think of
annotations.meaning: 那是她能想到的唯一办法
annotations.explain: the only way后接省略关系词的定语从句she could think of。
annotations.example: It was the only solution I could think of.

annotations.explain: once作连词，表示某事发生后；go missing表示失踪或下落不明。
annotations.example: Once the key went missing, everyone panicked.

annotations.explain: would的缩写'd描述过去视角下预期会发生的动作，非表示已查问。
annotations.example: The first person they'd call was the clerk.

annotations.explain: suck in a breath是小说常见的惊讶、震惊动作描写。
annotations.example: She sucked in a breath at the price.

annotations.explain: take a risk/risks表示冒险，such修饰名词短语强调程度。
annotations.example: Why would anyone take such a risk?

annotations.explain: instead of + doing表示以另一行为取代原动作。
annotations.example: Instead of arguing, she smiled.

annotations.phrase: drew an old prescription from her sleeve
annotations.explain: draw在文学叙事中也可表示抽出、取出物品，非画画。
annotations.example: He drew a letter from his pocket.

annotations.explain: be apprenticed at/to涉及拜师学艺或学徒经历；once在此为曾经。
annotations.example: She was apprenticed to a tailor.

annotations.phrase: tried to force him to testify
annotations.explain: force someone to do是强迫句型，try to do表示尝试，不能直接把未遂写成成功。
annotations.example: They tried to force her to sign.

annotations.explain: testify to可指证明某项事实，和testify against（作证指控）侧重点不同。
annotations.example: The witness testified to what she saw.

annotations.explain: ordeal指严酷经历或考验，escape可接名词直接表示幸免。
annotations.example: He escaped the worst of the storm.

annotations.explain: never + 过去式表示在所述时间范围内始终没有忘记，强调恩情持久。
annotations.example: She never forgot his kindness.

annotations.explain: repay a favor是固定表达，repay不仅用于还钱，也用于回报帮助。
annotations.example: I hope I can repay the favor someday.

annotations.explain: not entirely是部分否定，承认前述解释有道理但并不完整。
annotations.example: "Was it his fault?" "Not entirely."

annotations.explain: dare在此作实义动词，后面直接接原形动词（也可接to do）。
annotations.example: She never dared ask again.

annotations.explain: live on后接收入或食物，表示靠某项资源生活。
annotations.example: The family lives on one salary.

annotations.explain: there is/was no telling是固定习语，表示无法知道会发生什么。
annotations.example: There's no telling what might happen.

annotations.explain: pay the price既可字面付价款，也可比喻遭受后果。
annotations.example: Others shouldn't pay the price for his mistake.

annotations.explain: knock on指敲门窗等表面，times说明次数。
annotations.example: Someone knocked twice on the door.

annotations.explain: couldn't说明当时无能力或条件不允许，不等于主观不愿。
annotations.example: She couldn't leave her post.

annotations.explain: send someone to do表安排某人去完成某事。
annotations.example: They sent a driver to collect us.

annotations.explain: wait in强调位于某个空间内部，side alley指偏僻小巷。
annotations.example: I'll wait in the side street.

annotations.explain: hurry something over to是让物品尽快送达特定地点的叙事表达。
annotations.example: She hurried the files over to the office.

annotations.explain: under用于物体下方的位置；此处是递送消息的具体路径线索。
annotations.example: I found the key under the plate.

annotations.explain: through可表示通过某个中间人或渠道，而非仅穿过某处。
annotations.example: I heard the news through a friend.

annotations.explain: dare后可直接接动词原形，重点是害怕承担后果。
annotations.example: He didn't dare speak.

annotations.explain: click into place原指卡入正确位置，转指分散线索突然形成合理解释。
annotations.example: The details finally clicked into place.

annotations.explain: all along表示整个过程始终如此，不是“沿路”。
annotations.example: I knew the truth all along.

annotations.explain: mean to do表示有意做某事，与mean doing“意味着”不同。
annotations.example: I meant to tell you earlier.

annotations.explain: all + 从句 + was that强调知情范围有限，避免把推测当成事实。
annotations.example: All I knew was that the door was locked.

annotations.explain: plan to do表示有计划，不能据此推定行动已经实施。
annotations.example: They planned to leave at dawn.

annotations.phrase: planned to make you the bride
annotations.explain: make + 宾语 + 名词补语表示使某人具有特定身份或角色。
annotations.example: They made her team leader.

annotations.explain: that much指前述某一部分，体现角色只相信部分陈述。
annotations.example: That much I can confirm.

annotations.explain: with + 名词短语描写伴随的神态，chilly比cold更偏疏离感。
annotations.example: He answered with a chilly smile.

annotations.explain: not ... until强调某事延后才发生，用于凸显被隐瞒。
annotations.example: I didn't find out until Monday.

annotations.explain: practically在口语中可表示几乎、实际上，带夸张讽刺。
annotations.example: They practically pushed us out.

annotations.explain: won't/wouldn't在叙事中可表示拒绝或不肯做某事，meet someone's eyes指目光相接。
annotations.example: He wouldn't meet her eyes.

annotations.explain: refill作动词表示重新加满，refill + 饮料可作简洁文学描写。
annotations.example: She refilled my cup.

annotations.explain: 口语中don't even try常用于拒绝对方试图蒙混、说服或讨好。
annotations.example: Don't even try to blame me.

annotations.explain: make up for是补偿、弥补，不能与make up编造混淆。
annotations.example: A gift won't make up for the delay.

annotations.explain: Just then是小说常用时间转折，标志打断或新事件发生。
annotations.example: Just then, the bell rang.

annotations.explain: sharply副词使动作更急促、有力，塑造突发紧张感。
annotations.example: Someone knocked sharply at the door.

annotations.explain: in one's early/mid/late twenties表达大致年龄段，不等于精确年龄。
annotations.example: She's in her early twenties.

annotations.explain: callus是长期摩擦形成的茧，faint表示不明显；描绘人物劳动经历。
annotations.example: He had calluses on his hands.

annotations.explain: go + 颜色/形容词可表示状态变化，如go pale、go red。
annotations.example: His face went pale.

annotations.explain: shift指轮班，add强调数量增加，不代表已查明守卫是谁。
annotations.example: They added another night shift.

annotations.explain: handle既可指用手处理，也可指经办工作；everyone who是定语从句。
annotations.example: They checked everyone who handled the file.

annotations.explain: pass on表示转递消息或物品，常用于中间人。
annotations.example: Please pass on my thanks.

annotations.explain: crumpled为过去分词作形容词，暗示匆忙、慌乱。
annotations.example: He pulled out a crumpled receipt.

annotations.explain: plea是迫切请求；to be rescued是不定式被动结构。
annotations.example: It was a plea to be heard.

annotations.phrase: had a fever for three days
annotations.explain: have/has had + 持续时间表示持续到当前的状态，不能直接理解为三天前短暂发烧。
annotations.example: She's had a fever for two days.

annotations.explain: be out of表示某物已经用完，广泛用于日常生活。
annotations.example: We're out of milk.

annotations.explain: Who's是Who is的缩写，问身份；不问所有权。
annotations.example: Who's the new manager?

annotations.explain: for some time是未指明长度的持续时间表达。
annotations.example: He's been away for some time.

annotations.explain: quarters复数名词在此指居住区域，不是四分之一。
annotations.example: The staff live in nearby quarters.

annotations.explain: spring to mind是固定习语，指念头不由自主冒出来。
annotations.example: An old friend sprang to mind.

annotations.phrase: find some way to get them out
annotations.explain: find a way to do强调设法解决问题，get someone out使某人离开危险地点。
annotations.example: We need to find a way to get her out.

annotations.explain: jerk表示突然的急促动作，比raise更带惊吓或警觉。
annotations.example: His head jerked up at the sound.

annotations.phrase: What if you two get caught
annotations.explain: What if引导对风险的假设，get caught为get + 过去分词的被动式。
annotations.example: What if it rains tomorrow?

annotations.explain: lay–laid–laid意为放置；此处laid不是lie–lay–lain的过去式。
annotations.example: She laid a hand on my shoulder.

annotations.explain: when引导宾语从句，描述需要先查明的实际信息。
annotations.example: Find out when the shifts change.

annotations.phrase: gamble Nanny Zhou's whole family on a guess
annotations.meaning: 拿周嬷嬷全家去赌一个猜测
annotations.explain: gamble something on something比喻把重要的人或事押在不确定结果上，语气强烈。
annotations.example: Don't gamble your future on a rumor.

annotations.phrase: opened my mouth, then closed it
annotations.explain: 用并列动作代替直接写“无言以对”，是小说常用show, don't tell手法。
annotations.example: I opened my mouth, then thought better of it.

annotations.explain: look straight at表示直接注视，也可表达认真或质问。
annotations.example: She looked straight at me and waited.

annotations.phrase: what did you promise last time
annotations.explain: did you promise使用一般过去时询问先前作出的承诺。
annotations.example: What did you promise your parents?

annotations.explain: reluctantly是态度副词，表示勉强做某事，不是害羞。
annotations.example: He reluctantly agreed to help.

annotations.explain: decide for someone指代替他人做决定，此处凸显知情同意与自主权。
annotations.example: Ask her before deciding for her.

annotations.explain: do + 动词原形是肯定句中的强调助动词，表达确认或微妙讽刺。
annotations.example: I do understand your point.

annotations.explain: turn something over可以是翻面，也可表示移交；这里是翻到背面写字。
annotations.example: Turn the page over.

annotations.explain: find out + wh-从句用于调查尚不确定的信息。
annotations.example: Find out how much it costs.

annotations.explain: fever won't break是常见表达，break在此指发烧的持续状态终于终止。
annotations.example: Her fever finally broke at dawn.

annotations.explain: send for someone是派人去叫某人前来，不等于把大夫送出去。
annotations.example: Send for a doctor immediately.

annotations.explain: as for用于引入话题，whether引出两种可能性。
annotations.example: As for whether we go, we'll decide later.

annotations.explain: let + 宾语 + 动词原形，herself强调由当事人本人作答。
annotations.example: Let him explain it himself.

annotations.explain: right away是口语中立即的意思，否定突出犹豫。
annotations.example: She didn't answer right away.

annotations.explain: hesitantly显示不确定、顾虑，与reluctantly（不情愿）不同。
annotations.example: He spoke hesitantly at first.

annotations.phrase: what if she says she won't go
annotations.explain: what if引出尚未决定的假设风险；won't可表示不愿意。
annotations.example: What if they say no?

annotations.explain: glance at表示短暂看一眼，与stare at盯着看对照。
annotations.example: She glanced at the clock.

annotations.explain: start by + doing表示完成目标前先采取的第一步。
annotations.example: Start by checking the facts.

annotations.phrase: risking her life over a bowl of medicine
annotations.meaning: 为了一碗药冒生命危险
annotations.explain: risk one's life意为冒生命危险，over可表示因某事或围绕某事发生争执或冒险。
annotations.example: Don't risk your life over a rumor.

annotations.explain: tuck表示塞入或收好，介词in说明存放位置。
annotations.example: She tucked the note in her pocket.

annotations.phrase: harder than switching brides had been
annotations.explain: 过去完成时had been用于回顾更早发生的替嫁经历，than建立难度比较。
annotations.example: It was harder than I had expected.

annotations.explain: whether引导宾语从句，用于是或否的问题。
annotations.example: No one asked whether she agreed.

annotations.explain: climb into原指爬进，也可以用来形象表达进入车辆或狭窄空间。
annotations.example: She climbed into the carriage.

annotations.phrase: would have to start by asking
annotations.explain: would have to为过去叙事视角的将来必要性，start by + doing强调步骤。
annotations.example: We would have to start by checking.

annotations.explain: want to be + 过去分词是被动不定式，强调被救者本人是否愿意。
annotations.example: Ask whether they want to be involved.

scenes.title: 绣坊上门讨债
scenes.alt: 在温梨朴素的住处里，绣坊掌柜带着账单与旧绣样上门讨债，姜明月在一旁旁观。

scenes.title: 协商分期还款
scenes.alt: 温梨为绣坊掌柜添茶，提出首付与分月偿还的方案，桌上摆着旧绣样和账契。

scenes.title: 两百两坦白
scenes.alt: 夜色与花影下，姜明月向温梨坦白母亲收下两百两银子的事，气氛克制而沉重。

scenes.title: 刑部收讫凭据
scenes.alt: 春桃送来刑部的收讫纸张，温梨与姜明月一起查看，明白收讫并不等于无罪定论。

scenes.title: 周嬷嬷的三角纸条
scenes.alt: 温梨关窗后取出折成三角的小纸条，姜明月凑近细看，两人神色凝重。

scenes.title: 阿芹赶来报信
scenes.alt: 年轻绣坊女伙计阿芹匆匆赶来，双手递出揉皱的纸条，温梨与姜明月神情紧张。

scenes.title: 药方背面写回信
scenes.alt: 温梨在旧药方背面写给阿芹的回话，姜明月在旁深思，筹划谨慎的营救。
